summary: parks.ca.gov page + 2011 brochure + RC + imagery read. TEMPORARILY CLOSED (flooding and high swells, page checked 11/27/2026). 10 primitive first-come sites, chemical toilets, no water, RVs to ~28 ft. Not on ReserveCalifornia. No fee found. Waterfront riverfront looks wrong (lagoon 80-90 m at image time; this is an ocean beach camp) - coastal walk recommended. Open-beach-sand question flagged. Phone unchanged.
flags: STATUS: temporarily_closed - 'Navarro Beach is closed due to flooding and high swells CA State Parks will be monitoring the area and will open it once it is safe.' (parks.ca.gov page_id=435, last checked 11/27/2026). No reopening date.

WATERFRONT riverfront -> coastal walk recommended (report only, not applied). The parking spaces (~39.1918,-123.7584 to 39.1905,-123.7581, no site numbers posted) line the back of the open ocean beach at the river mouth; on Esri imagery the river lagoon is ~80-90 m NW across open sand (stored evidence said ~50 m) and the surf ~180 m SW over the camp's own beach, no road, town or other use between. Not coastal dunes (open beach and driftwood, no dune field). Riverfront fails the ~50 m test at image time; riverview is the alternative if the ocean value is not wanted. Suggested evidence: 'Esri 2026-11-27: parking-space camp along the back of the open ocean beach at the Navarro River mouth, surf ~180 m over the park's own beach, lagoon 80-90 m; no road or other use between -> coastal walk'.

EKKO SAND QUESTION (unsettled, for AWH): the spaces are on the beach backshore at the foot of the bluff, at the end of the access road. Imagery shows a lighter packed-looking strip where the vehicles stand but cannot tell packed gravel/sand from bare beach sand. The agency calls them 'parking spaces' that 'accommodate RVs up to 28 feet' (brochure) and lists 'RV Access'. Not dropped.

RIG LENGTH: the park page's 'Max trailer: 24 feet / Max camper/motorhome: 30 feet' is park-wide (also covers Paul M. Dimmick, 11677); the brochure says 28 ft for Navarro Beach. A 23-ft rig fits either way.
FEES: no current fee published on the park page or ReserveCalifornia; fees left unknown.
